output.summary: The PIIA Clause 8.1 assigns all rights to software related to distributed tracing/observability created during employment, regardless of hours or hardware. TraceLite, an existing Apache-2.0 library maintained off-hours on personal hardware, falls under this scope. Clause 8.3's 'None' exclusion is pending review with no state carve-out, and post-start maintenance of prior codebases is explicitly covered by 8.1, creating a potential conflict with the user's goal.
key_claims: PIIA Clause 8.1 assigns all rights to software related to distributed tracing/observability created during employment, regardless of hours or hardware
TraceLite is an existing Apache-2.0 library maintained off-hours on personal hardware
Post-start maintenance of prior codebases falls under Clause 8.1
risks_or_flaws: PIIA Clause 8.1 explicitly claims ownership of TraceLite and personal off-hours tools related to distributed tracing/observability
Exhibit A's 'None' exclusion is pending review with no state carve-out, creating uncertainty about prior inventions
output.verification_question: Does 'during employment' in Clause 8.1 include off-hours work on personal hardware for projects related to distributed tracing/observability?
